# flutter_constraint_layout

> A faithful port of Android ConstraintLayout to Flutter, in pure Dart. Every child is a direct child of one `ConstraintLayout`, and each child declares where its edges go (pinned to the parent or to a sibling by id) and how it is sized. The widget tree stays flat instead of nesting rows, columns, and stacks, and the same layout runs on iOS, Android, web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.

flutter_constraint_layout is pure Dart (no native code, no platform setup) and runs on every Flutter platform. Add it with `flutter pub add flutter_constraint_layout` (or `flutter_constraint_layout: ^1.0.0` under `dependencies` in `pubspec.yaml`) and import `package:flutter_constraint_layout/flutter_constraint_layout.dart`, which brings in every widget, dimension, link, and helper. It requires Dart 3.12 or newer and Flutter 3.44 or newer, and its API is designed around Dart dot shorthands. Children are declared with the `Constrained` widget, each keyed by a `Symbol` id, and positioned with dot-shorthand constraints such as `.startOf(parent, margin: 16)`, `.fixed(56)`, `.matchConstraint`, `.percent(0.5)`, `.spread`, `.packed`, and `.gone`. Helpers like `Guideline` and `Barrier`, chains, aspect ratios, circular positioning, and the virtual `ConstraintFlow` and `ConstraintGrid` layouts cover the arrangements that usually require extra wrapper widgets. Under the hood a deterministic dependency-graph resolver handles most layouts and falls back to a slower Cassowary constraint solver for the rest, such as a layout with a barrier, a circular link, a `ConstraintFlow` or `ConstraintGrid`, or a chain with a gone or aspect-ratio member. The engine is a line-faithful port of androidx constraintlayout core whose resolver is verified at parity with core 1.1.1.

**Read the full documentation first.** The single file below contains the complete, authoritative docs (installation, anchoring edges, bias and centering, constraint dimensions, aspect ratios, chains, guidelines, barriers, circular positioning, visibility and gone, the virtual Flow and Grid layouts, a worked example, and the engine internals). Fetch it before answering questions about this package: it is compact, self-contained Markdown written to be read in one pass.

## Docs

- [Complete flutter_constraint_layout documentation (Markdown)](https://constraints.birju.dev/docs.md): The entire docs page as one Markdown file. Fetch and read this in full for accurate API usage, constraint syntax, code examples, and layout patterns. This is the most reliable source; prefer it over guessing.

## Reference

- [Package on pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_constraint_layout): Versions, API reference, and install instructions.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/constraint_layout): Repository, issues, and changelog.
- [Live documentation site](https://constraints.birju.dev/docs): The interactive docs, with every example rendered live beside its code.

## Optional

- [flutter_constraint_layout_lints](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/constraint_layout/tree/main/packages/flutter_constraint_layout_lints): An analyzer plugin that warns about duplicate and undefined constraint ids (`duplicate_constraint_id`, `undefined_constraint_id`).
- [constraint_engine](https://github.com/BirjuVachhani/constraint_layout/tree/main/packages/constraint_engine): The pure-Dart layout engine underneath, with no Flutter dependency.
- [Android ConstraintLayout (upstream)](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/layout/constraint-layout): The original Android layout this package ports; constraint concepts and behavior match it.
- [androidx constraintlayout core](https://github.com/androidx/constraintlayout): The Java source the layout engine is ported from.
